===[[Pokémon Masters EX]]===
{{main|Ash (Masters)}}
Ash, in his {{aniseries|JN}} design, forms a [[sync pair]] with {{AP|Pikachu}} in [[Pokémon Masters EX]]. Ash became a playable sync pair on August 28, 2022.

In this game, Ash accidentally wound up on [[Pasio]] while training for the [[Masters Eight Tournament]]. He first appeared as an NPC during the [[special event]] {{DL|Special event|The Classic Thunderbolt}}. Ash was also shown to pair alongside the other members of his ''Pokémon Journeys'' team, which could be battled during the {{DL|Special event|Challenge from Ash}} event.

==Quotes==
{{main|Ash Ketchum/Quotes}}

==In the manga==
===The Electric Tale of Pikachu===
{{main|Ash Ketchum (EToP)}}
Ash is a starring character in [[The Electric Tale of Pikachu]], which is based on {{aniseries|OS}}. His journey follows roughly the same plot as in ''Pokémon the Series: The Beginning'': first traveling the [[Kanto]] region to participate in the [[Indigo Plateau Conference|Pokémon League]], before embarking on a journey around the [[Orange Islands]].

[[File:DP series trio.png|thumb|left|200px|Ash with his friends in the movie 10 manga adaptation]]
[[File:Ash and Brock MPJ.png|thumb|200px|Ash and Brock in [[Magical Pokémon Journey]]]]
===Movie adaptations===
Since Ash and his Pikachu have appeared in every Pokémon movie to date, likewise, Ash is the main character in every movie manga adaptation. The same applies to Ash's team as they made similar appearances.

===Magical Pokémon Journey===
Ash, along with {{an|Misty}} and {{an|Brock}}, made cameo appearances in bonus chapters of [[Magical Pokémon Journey]]. In them, Ash and {{ashfr}} have mistakenly wandered into the world Magical Pokémon Journey is set in. The bonus chapters chronicle their attempts to return to their world (of the animated series) and their encounters with various aspects of the Magical Pokémon Journey [[canon]] which differ from the animated series canon (such as the use of [[Poké Ball]]s).
{{-}}

===Ash & Pikachu===
[[File:Ash Ketchum AP.png|thumb|200px|Ash in Ash & Pikachu]]
[[File:Ash Ketchum 2 AP.png|thumb|left|200px|Ash in his Hoenn attire in Ash & Pikachu]]
Ash is the main protagonist of [[Ash & Pikachu]], which is based on {{aniseries|GS}} and {{aniseries|RS}}, adapting episode plots from the [[Johto]], [[Hoenn]], and {{gdis|Battle Frontier|III}} sagas.

However, instead of following the plot of the series, this manga follows Ash and Dawn going through various experiences with the Pokémon they encounter while traveling together.

==In the TCG==
[[File:AshFriendshipAshvsTeamRocketDeck25.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{TCG ID|Ash vs Team Rocket Deck|Ash's Friendship|25}}, the only Supporter card depicting Ash]]

Ash Ketchum and his Pokémon have made sporadic appearances as cards in the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]], many of which have not been released outside of Japan. Usually, these cards are released alongside [[Pokémon movie]]s.

The first TCG card featuring Pokémon that Ash possesses was a [[jumbo card|jumbo]] {{TCG|Unnumbered Promotional cards|promo card}} for his [[Ash's Pikachu|Pikachu]] teamed up with the [[Pichu Brothers]], which was [[Pichu and Pikachu (CoroCoro promo)|Pichu and Pikachu]]. It was a tie in to ''[[PK07|Pikachu and Pichu]]'', one of the [[Pikachu short]]s. The first card released at normal size and the first that features Ash in the card artwork was {{TCG ID|ADV-P Promo|Ash's Treecko|36}}, released as a promotional card. This card is also the first that features "Ash's" as a prefix, making it and other cards like it mechanically [[Owner's Pokémon]].

[[File:StaraptorMMovieRandomPack18.jpg|thumb|200px|left|[[Staraptor M (Movie Random Pack 18)|Staraptor]]{{SP|M}}, an example of a Pokémon card featuring Ash Ketchum]]
During the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game#Diamond & Pearl Series|Diamond & Pearl Series]], cards featuring Pokémon that Ash possesses are released as [[Pokémon M]], a group of [[Pokémon SP]] based on the Pokémon seen in Pokémon movies which were released in the {{TCG|Movie Commemoration Random Pack}} to promote ''[[M12|Arceus and the Jewel of Life]]''. Mechanically, these cards are not considered "Owner's  Pokémon" cards due to the naming scheme, despite the similar styling and the appearance of Ash on the card art. There are two such cards, namely [[Pikachu M (Movie Random Pack 12)|Pikachu]]{{SP|M}} for Ash's Pikachu and [[Staraptor M (Movie Random Pack 18)|Staraptor]]{{SP|M}} for [[Ash's Staraptor]]. A third card, [[Pikachu M LV.X (DPt-P Promo 43)|Pikachu]]{{SP|M}} [[Pikachu M LV.X (DPt-P Promo 43)|LV.X]], was released as [[DPt-P Promotional cards|DPt-P Promotional card]] alongside the set and is a {{TCG|Pokémon LV.X|Level Up}} for the Pikachu{{SP|M}} card.

In the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game#Black & White Series|Black & White Series]], an event tied to the distribution of [[List of local English event Pokémon distributions in Generation V#Secret Eggs|Secret Eggs]] which had the possibility of hatching into a {{p|Pidove}} based on [[Ash's Pidove]] (among other main characters' Pokémon) also involved the release of a {{TCG|BW Black Star Promos|BW Black Star Promo}} {{TCG ID|BW Promo|Pidove|15}}. In the XY Series, an [[Ash-Greninja-EX (XY Promo 133)|Ash-Greninja]]{{EX}} was released. It showcased [[Ash-Greninja]], a new form that [[Ash's Greninja]] could take on in the show during [[S19|Pokémon the Series: XYZ]] that resembles Ash himself. Both of these cards received English releases.

[[File:AshPikachuGXAshVSTeamRocketDeckKit5.jpg|thumb|200px|right|[[Ash's Pikachu-GX (Ash vs Team Rocket Deck 5)|Ash's Pikachu]]{{GX}}, an example of an "Ash's Pokémon" card. This card also interacts with the aforementioned Ash's Friendship Supporter card]]
The [[Pokémon Trading Card Game#Sun & Moon Series|Sun & Moon Series]] has Ash's most prominent appearances in the TCG to date. The {{TCG|Ash vs Team Rocket Deck Kit}} included a complete half deck themed around Ash Ketchum, with many Pokémon cards having artwork related to Ash's adventures in [[Alola]] during {{aniseries|SM}}. The only card in this half deck that is mechanically considered an "Ash's Pokémon" is [[Ash's Pikachu-GX (Ash vs Team Rocket Deck 5)|Ash's Pikachu]]{{GX}}. The half deck also introduces Ash Ketchum himself as a Supporter card named {{TCG ID|Ash vs Team Rocket Deck|Ash's Friendship|25}}. Its effect causes the user to draw two cards, but instead draws four cards if that player also has Ash's Pikachu{{GX}} in play. A card for [[Ash's Litten]], {{TCG ID|SM-P Promo|Litten|59}}, was released as a promotional card alongside the deck kit, which also has Ash in its artwork.

Ash's Pikachu would be printed seven more times in the Sun & Moon Series, this time as {{TCG|SM Black Star Promos}} representing the various [[Pikachu in a cap|Ash's Pikachu forms]]. These cards, as with the entire promotion surrounding the forms, were a tie in to the movie ''[[M20|I Choose You!]]''. Each one wears one of [[Ash's hat]]s from across {{aniseries|PTS}}. These cards also received an English language release.

Lastly, a card representing Ash's Pikachu, {{TCG ID|SM Promo|Pikachu|227}}, was printed as SM Black Star Promo, with its basis being the movie ''[[M22|Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution]]''. While this card did receive an English printing, a printing with art including Ash Ketchum was only used in Japan.

This listing is of cards mentioning or featuring Ash or his Pokémon in the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]].

==Trivia==
[[File:Ash hat OS concept art.jpg|thumb|200px|Concept art of Ash's hat from the original series]]
[[File:Ash Dewgong Drawing.png|thumb|200px|Ash's drawing of a Dewgong]]
* Ash was designed by [[Atsuko Nishida]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/El_Aleph87/status/1632063563744378884 Press release of "Hometown Story"]</ref>
* Ash's height is around 4'7" (140&nbsp;cm).<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20210219050737/https://pokemonday.pokemon.co.jp/tips/065/ Japanese Pokémon Day website tip #65] (Archived)</ref>
* [[Ash's hat]] in the [[original series]] was similar to {{ga|Red}}'s hat in his original design from {{game|Red and Green|s}} before undergoing several changes until the final design.
* Ash is still considered a 10-year-old in promotional materials and in mainline animated series episodes as recent as ''[[JN067|Sleuths for Truth!]]'', despite at least a year having been implied to have passed between ''[[EP158|A Goldenrod Opportunity]]'' and ''[[BW141|Best Wishes Until We Meet Again!]]''.
** [[Kunihiko Yuyama]], creative supervisor for {{aniseries|JN}} and executive director for prior series, has stated in an interview with {{wp|Daniel Arsham}} in ''Arsham's Pokédex'', a collection of Pokémon-related artwork, that Ash does not age because the animated series is set in an endless early summer.
* When [[Veronica Taylor]] was interviewed in the documentary "Adventures in Voice Acting", she stated that during her audition for the role of Ash, he was known as Casey at the time. This name would later be given to a {{an|Casey|recurring character from Johto}}.
* Ash originally wanted a {{p|Squirtle}} to be his [[first partner Pokémon]], but {{an|Professor Oak}} told him it was taken by a [[Gary Oak|Trainer who was not late]].
* In the animated series, Ash is the first and, so far, only [[Pokémon Trainer]]:
** With a known [[hometown]] to not be native to any of the regions he is the {{pkmn|Champion}} of.
** With access to [[Z-Move]]s, [[Dynamax]]/[[Gigantamax]], and [[Mega Evolution]] at the same time.
*** Who has used more than one of those in a single battle.
** Shown to have won two of the same Gym Badge, as he's earned a {{badge|Rain}} from both [[Juan]] and [[Wallace]].
* Ash is the only Champion in the animated series to own a [[Mythical Pokémon]].
* Ash has never caught another Electric-type Pokémon other than Pikachu.
* Ash has never officially owned a {{cat|female-only Pokémon}}.
** While he has technically owned a [[Legendary Pokémon]] in {{AP|Solgaleo}}, he has never officially {{pkmn2|caught}} one in a [[Poké Ball]].
* Ash has caught at least one of the [[first partner Pokémon]] of every [[region]] he has visited, except for [[Galar]].
* As of ''[[JN016|A Chilling Curse!]]'', Ash has caught at least one Pokémon belonging to all eighteen [[type]]s (this includes Pokémon he owns or has owned that have been retroactively made {{type|Fairy}}).
** Also, as of ''[[JN099|Battling Turned Up to Eleven!]]'', he has used at least one [[move]] of every type with his Pokémon.
* Ash has caught at least one {{type|Flying}} Pokémon in every [[series]].
** Moreover, Flying is the most common type among Ash's non-temporary Pokémon under his ownership, with a total of twelve representants.
* [[Alola]] is the only region in which Ash does not catch a {{type|Water}} Pokémon.
** Similarly, ''Pokémon Journeys: The Series'' is the only series in which he does not catch a {{type|Fire}} Pokémon.
* All of Ash's {{type|Grass}} Pokémon are part of a three-stage evolutionary line.
* Ash's favorite move is {{m|Thunderbolt}}, as revealed by himself in ''[[XY025|Climbing the Walls!]]''.
* Ash can {{wp|drawing|draw}}, as shown in ''[[DP089|Up Close and Personable!]]'' when he drew a {{p|Dewgong}}. However, his drawing was insulted by [[Angie]].
* Ash has been shown to be a good climber at various points in the animated series, such as in ''[[BW002|Enter Iris and Axew!]]'', ''Climbing the Walls'', and ''[[SM075|Some Kind of Laziness!]]'', to the point of {{an|Misty}} saying "He climbs like a {{p|Mankey}}" in ''[[M04|Celebi: The Voice of the Forest]]'', and {{an|Brock}} calling him a "human {{p|Aipom}}" in ''[[M08|Lucario and the Mystery of Mew]]''.
* Ash has lost once to every {{type|Normal}} [[Gym Leader]] he has met. Out of the four Normal-type Gym Leaders he has battled against, [[Cheren]] is the only one against whom Ash has never won.
* The only region where Ash didn't lose any official Gym battles is the [[Orange Islands|Orange Archipelago]].
** Also, Ash did not lose any official trials in {{aniseries|SM}}, although he lost to [[Nanu]] in an [[SM074|unofficial battle]].
* Ever since facing [[Wattson]] in ''[[AG040|Watt's with Wattson?]]'', Ash has not won a Gym [[Badge]] in the same episode in which he meets the [[Gym Leader]].
* If only {{pkmn|Trainer}} battles are counted, Ash's longest winning streak lasted a total of 87 episodes, spanning from his loss to [[Rinto]] in ''[[JN051|Trials of a Budding Master!]]'' to his loss to Misty in ''[[JN138|A Fated Face-Off!]]''.
** If not, as all of his eligible Pokémon were defeated in a [[Raid Battle (GO)#In animation|Raid Battle]] against an {{p|Articuno}} in ''[[JN102|Battling in the Freezing Raid!]]'', the longest period Ash has been on a winning streak is exactly 70 episodes, going from ''[[XY036|Battles in the Sky!]]'' to ''[[XY106|A Meeting of Two Journeys!]]''.
* Ash has defeated more regional Champions onscreen in the animated series than any other Trainer, having won official battles against {{an|Iris}}, {{an|Steven Stone|Steven}}, {{an|Cynthia}}, and {{an|Leon}}, as well as an unofficial battle against [[Alder]], who fell asleep before the battle began and forfeited soon after waking up.
** Additionally, he has defeated Wallace, the former [[Hoenn]] Champion.
* Ash shares at least one Pokémon of the same evolutionary line with one of his rivals in each series.
* ''[[JN032|Time After Time!]]'' and ''[[JN133|The Mew from Here!]]'' are the only mainline animated series episodes of {{aniseries|PTS}} to not feature Ash in any capacity.
* In promotional material for the [[Manalo Conference]], Ash was given the title of (Japanese: ゼンリョクチャレンジャ ''Full-force challenger'').
* {{DL|Pokémon social media|National Ash Ketchum Day}} is celebrated every September 15, the anniversary of Ash's first [[Pokémon League Conference]] [[SM139|victory]], first being celebrated on said victory's first-year anniversary in 2020.
* In the [[Pokémon: Twilight Wings]] episode ''[[TW01|Letter]]'', a Trainer who bears a resemblance to Ash can be seen at the entrance to [[Wyndon Stadium]] with a {{p|Pikachu}}.
* Although Ash has been retired from the role of main protagonist as of {{aniseries|HZ}}, Senior Marketing Director of [[The Pokémon Company International]], Andy Gose, has not ruled out the possibility of him reappearing at some point due to him still being around in the world of Pokémon.<ref>[https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/pokemon-horizons-netflix-ash-ketchum-1235927798/?utm_source=syndication Variety]</ref>
* In [[Pokémon Legends: Z-A]], [[Mission (Legends: Z-A)#Side mission|Side Mission 107]]: "The World's Greatest Pikachu!" is requested by a {{tc|Grade-Schooler}} named Pikami, who uses only a {{p|Pikachu}} and whose attire resembles that of Ash, likely being a reference.
* In the licensed Brazilian music video "[[The Strength of the Master]]", a boy and a girl appear dressed as Ash and Misty.
